title: The State of American Friendship: Change, Challenges, and Loss (plus companion piece 'Men's Social Circles are Shrinking')
author: Daniel A. Cox
publication: Survey Center on American Life (American Enterprise Institute)
accessedVia: curl direct HTML fetch + custom tag-stripping script (Python), byte-verbatim body text; the appended 'Men's Social Circles are Shrinking' supplementary block (same URL family: https://www.americansurveycenter.org/why-mens-social-circles-are-shrinking/) was captured via the WebFetch tool's extraction rather than raw HTML parse, and is flagged inline in raw-01.txt as such
notes: Primary survey report, TARGET 1. Underlying instrument: May 2021 American Perspectives Survey (APS), n=2,019 US adults 18+, Ipsos KnowledgePanel probability panel, fielded May 14-23 2021, MOE +/-2.4pp at 95% CI, design effect 1.2. Contains the exact narrative sentence for the 41%-women/21%-men emotional-support figure with 'in the past week' recall window explicitly stated. Does NOT contain the literal interviewer-facing question text (that lives in the topline PDF, which was not machine-readable in this environment -- see GAP in evidence-notes.md). Footnote [4] flags a wording caveat on the 1990 Gallup comparison (husband/wife only vs. spouse/partner). Footnote [7] flags a mode-effect caveat (phone 1990 vs. online 2021) on the close-friends-count trend. The appended supplementary block sources the sex-split 'six or more close friends, 1990 vs today' and 'no close friends' figures, which do NOT appear broken out by sex in the main report page itself.

title: Men, Women and Social Connections (report landing page + Chapter 2: 'Where men and women turn for emotional support and social connection')
author: Isabel Goddard and Kim Parker
accessedVia: curl direct HTML fetch + custom tag-stripping script (Python), byte-verbatim body text, two pages of the same report combined
notes: Primary survey report, TARGET 2 -- the single most direct instrumented test found for the 'do men favor partner over other channels more than women do' question. Underlying instrument: Pew American Trends Panel (ATP) Wave 154 + SSRS Opinion Panel oversample, n=6,204 US adults, fielded Sept 3-15 2024, probability-based address-recruited panels. KEY RESULT: 'Men and women are equally likely to say they'd lean on their spouse or partner' for emotional support (74% overall extremely/very likely) -- i.e. no sex gap in stated partner-reliance. The sex gap that DOES exist is in breadth of OTHER channels (mother, friend, other family, professional), all higher for women. Also contains a same-topic figure that sits in tension with raw-01.txt: 'men and women are about equally likely to say they have at least one close friend' (2024 Pew) vs. the 2021 ASC sex-split showing men much more likely to have zero close friends -- different surveys/instruments/years, flagged inline, not merged.
